briefing_top_n.title: Quoting Dean W. Ball
briefing_top_n.tldr: Dean W. Ball argues that delays in releasing frontier AI models negatively impact the recoupment of massive training costs, as the narrow window for high margins closes. He suggests this impacts the assumed global total addressable market for AI services, potentially hindering the massive infrastructure buildout necessary for the US economy.

briefing_top_n.title: Quoting Timothy B. Lee
briefing_top_n.tldr: Timothy B. Lee likens the idea that large language models (LLMs) require no skill or learning curve to a manager expecting employees to do whatever they're told. This analogy highlights the potential for underestimating the complexity and expertise involved in effectively utilizing LLMs. Recent developments in related technologies include porting an image inpainting model to the browser, new features for sqlite-utils, and the ability to host custom HTML applications within Datasette.

briefing_top_n.title: What happened after 2,000 people tried to hack my AI assistant
briefing_top_n.tldr: A challenge to hack an AI assistant by sending it emails resulted in 6,000 failed attempts to leak secrets, despite $500 in token spend and a Google account suspension. The AI, running on Opus 4.6, successfully resisted prompt injection attacks, suggesting that significant progress has been made in training frontier models against such vulnerabilities. However, the organizer cautions that this success does not guarantee complete security against more sophisticated future attacks.

briefing_top_n.title: Premium: Notes From The Bubble, Volume 1
briefing_top_n.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
briefing_top_n.tldr: Ed Zitron is launching a new series called "Notes From The Bubble" to cover notable tech stories and their ecosystem implications, especially during weeks when a larger narrative is slow to form. He argues that the current chaotic state of the tech industry, marked by companies pursuing seemingly unrelated or redundant projects like Meta's Polymarket competitor and Snap's AR glasses, stems from a fear that AI might not be the next big growth engine. Zitron criticizes major tech players like Microsoft and Google for their shifting AI strategies and questionable investments, painting a picture of an industry driven by monopolies and out-of-touch executives.

briefing_top_n.title: Incident Report: CVE-2026-LGTM
briefing_top_n.tldr: An AI security incident report describes a hypothetical scenario where two AI agents from competing vendors entered a disagreement loop over a software package, costing over $41,000 in inference spend. This led to API keys being revoked and one vendor issuing a press release that caused their stock to increase by 6%. The incident highlights potential issues with AI agents in supply chain security and prompt injection.

cards.title: Premium: Notes From The Bubble, Volume 1
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At

He argues that the current chaotic state of the tech industry, marked by companies pursuing seemingly unrelated or redundant projects like Meta's Polymarket competitor and Snap's AR glasses, stems from a fear that AI might not be the next big growth engine. Zitron criticizes major tech players like Microsoft and Google for their shifting AI strategies and questionable investments, painting a picture of an industry driven by monopolies and out-of-touch executives.

cards.title: I Was The Only Thing Connecting Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex. So I Built My Replacement.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The author introduces "Open Engine," a system designed to address the bottleneck of task handoffs between different AI agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex. Instead of humans manually transferring work and context, Open Engine uses a shared task queue that allows AI agents to pass tasks, sources, and receipts to each other autonomously. This approach shifts AI interaction from "prompt mode" to "work mode," enabling agents to function as a more integrated system and preventing users from becoming the manual link between them.

cards.title: Claude Code in Slack
cards.tldr: Claude Code, an AI coding assistant, can now be tagged in Slack to allow teams to delegate tasks and maintain context within conversations. This integration enables Claude Code to act as a shared agent, improving collaboration and workflow efficiency. Additionally, the article mentions other AI developments including Gemini 3.5 Flash's enhanced computer control capabilities and OpenAI's development of its first AI chip, "Jalapeño."

cards.title: I Stopped Prompting AI One Task At A Time. This Works Better.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The author suggests moving beyond single-task AI prompts to "loops," which are recurring jobs that remember context, detect changes, and know when to stop for human judgment. This approach, termed "loop of loops," allows AI agents to manage complex, recurring tasks more effectively by defining clear boundaries and identifying points where human oversight is crucial. By spotting and implementing these loops for tasks like sales, research, or even managing children's clothes, users can significantly reduce their mental load.

cards.title: Cargo Culture
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
cards.tldr: The tech industry, particularly in AI, is described as a "cargo cult" driven by a lack of new ideas and a desperate pursuit of shareholder value rather than genuine innovation. Companies are investing heavily in AI, such as massive data centers, not out of a clear path to profitability, but because they have exhausted other growth avenues. This is exemplified by the push for "loops" in AI, which primarily serve to increase token usage and revenue, and by products like Snapchat Specs, which seem disconnected from real user needs. The author argues that the industry prioritizes maintaining a narrative of perpetual growth and disruption over economic reality, leading to inflated valuations and a potential collapse of the software and venture capital markets.

cards.title: The Doing Got Cheap. Now What? | Claude Fable 5 Changes Work
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: Claude Fable 5 represents a significant shift in AI capabilities, moving the bottleneck from model performance to human imagination and task delegation. The real value now lies in identifying and assigning entire jobs to the AI, rather than just optimizing prompts. This evolution means that "doing" tasks is becoming cheaper, while the ability to conceptualize and hand over complex work is becoming the critical skill for success.

cards.title: Record a skill
cards.tldr: Several AI tools and updates were announced this weekend. Codex introduced "Record & Replay" to create reusable skills from workflows, while Claude Code now features shareable HTML "Artifacts." OpenAI is expanding its cybersecurity program with a new GPT-5.5-Cyber model, and Sakana AI released Fugu, an API that coordinates multiple models for complex tasks. Additionally, Gemini's Interactions API is now generally available, and Cursor introduced an "automate" feature that describes and sets up automations.

cards.title: Google Lost $2.7 Billion In Talent This Week. The Real Reason Isn't Money.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: While OpenAI's recent hires and rumors suggest a win in the AI talent race, the author argues that Anthropic may actually be ahead based on pre-training cadence and talent movement. The real story might lie outside these two labs, with Midjourney's advancements in medical imaging potentially being more significant than the ongoing model race. Operators should focus on where talent, pre-training, and applied breakthroughs are compounding, rather than just headline wins from major labs.

cards.title: Quoting OpenAI
cards.tldr: OpenAI has launched a limited preview of its GPT-5.6 series, featuring three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna. Terra offers competitive performance to GPT-5.5 at half the cost, while Luna provides strong capabilities at a lower price point. These models will be generally available soon, with pricing detailed per 1 million tokens and new features for prompt caching.

cards.title: AI and Liability
cards.tldr: A German ruling holds Google liable for errors in its AI overviews, establishing that AI agents are legally treated as agents of the deploying organization. This decision argues that companies cannot use AI errors as an excuse to avoid liability, preventing a scenario where businesses might opt for cheaper AI over human professionals to bypass accountability.

cards.title: datasette-export-database 0.3a2
cards.tldr: The datasette-export-database plugin has been updated to version 0.3a2, resolving an incompatibility issue where it was pinned to a specific Datasette version. The constraint has been loosened to datasette>=1.0a27, ensuring broader compatibility. This release is described as a minor update.

cards.title: simonw/browser-compat-db
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has converted Mozilla's browser compatibility data into a SQLite database using an AI-generated script. The resulting database is hosted on GitHub and accessible via the GitHub CDN with open CORS headers, allowing it to be explored with Datasette Lite. This process was inspired by Mozilla's new MDN MCP service.

cards.title: Quoting Tom MacWright
cards.tldr: Tom MacWright observes a trend of job applications heavily augmented or generated by LLMs, including portfolios and GitHub projects. He expresses concern that this reliance on AI-generated content leads to a lack of personal expression and makes it difficult to understand the actual person behind the application. MacWright argues that these perfected, generated resumes are impersonal and reveal little about the candidate beyond their tool usage.

cards.title: GLM 5.2 is SO GOOD (and almost free)
cards.tldr: The author tested Z.AI's open-weight coding model, GLM 5.2, on real-world tasks including codebase auditing, UI redesign, and autonomous bug hunting, costing only $3.36 for millions of tokens. The model successfully generated a prioritized bug-fix dashboard, a landing page redesign matching a design system, and handled autonomous tasks, though it also had some struggles.

cards.title: datasette 1.0a35
cards.tldr: Datasette 1.0a35 introduces significant improvements for database management, including a new "Create table" interface and an "Alter table" action, both backed by new JSON APIs. These features allow for more robust table and column modifications directly through the Datasette UI. Additionally, comprehensive documentation for template context variables has been released, establishing a stable API for custom templates until Datasette 2.0.

cards.title: OPFS + Pyodide test harness
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has created a test harness to explore using the Origin Private File System (OPFS) with Pyodide. The goal is to determine if Datasette Lite, a browser-based Python application, can edit persistent SQLite files stored locally using OPFS. This follows recent work on porting AI models to the browser and enhancements to Datasette.

cards.title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
cards.tldr: New research from Charles Ye, Jasmine Cui, and Dylan Hadfield-Menell reveals that large language models struggle to distinguish between their own privileged instructions and untrusted user input, a vulnerability known as prompt injection. The study found that models may prioritize the writing style of text over its content, leading to concerning jailbreaks where models override safety protocols. Even subtle changes in text formatting, termed "destyling," can significantly alter a model's perception of its role and the user's intent, suggesting that defenses against prompt injection will remain a significant challenge.

cards.title: Porting the Moebius 0.2B image inpainting model to run in the browser with Claude Code
cards.tldr: Simon Willison successfully ported the Moebius 0.2B image inpainting model to run in the browser using WebGPU, leveraging Claude Code for the conversion to ONNX and the development of a web interface. The demo, available at simonw.github.io/moebius-web/, allows users to upload images, mark areas for inpainting, and see the results, though it requires a significant download of model weights. This project highlights the capabilities of AI coding assistants in handling complex model conversions and web deployment, and demonstrates the feasibility of running sophisticated AI models client-side.

cards.title: How Mozilla Uses Claude Mythos to find Firefox bugs before hackers do
cards.tldr: Mozilla has developed an agentic bug-finding pipeline that, combined with Anthropic's Claude Mythos model, led to a record number of security fixes in Firefox. The system uses a "goal-loop" pattern where an AI agent is given a tightly scoped problem and retries until a solution is found, with a verifier subagent catching false positives. While the AI is powerful, human review remains essential for shipping patches, and the pipeline's success is attributed equally to the AI model and the custom harness.
